name: Federal Republic of Central America
native: Provincias Unidas del Centro de America

predecessors.name: First Mexican Empire
predecessors.text: Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica: the Central American provinces 'between the 8th and 18th parallel north'

successors.name: Guatemala
successors.text: Guatemala, whose president Rafael Carrera issued the decree of 17 April 1839 dissolving the federation

successors.name: Republic of El Salvador
successors.text: El Salvador, which 'declared independence from the Federal Republic of Central America' on 30 January 1841

successors.name: Republic of Costa Rica
successors.text: Costa Rica, seceded 15 November 1838 (and from 1 April 1829 to February 1831)

ledger.x: 1823: Central America declares independence from Mexico.
1824: the constitution makes the Federal Republic of Central America.
1831: Costa Rica rejoins the federation in February.
1834: the federal capital moves from Guatemala City to Sonsonate on 5 February and to San Salvador in June.
1838: Costa Rica secedes for the second time on 15 November.

wars.name: Central American civil war of 1827-1829
wars.outcome: Morazan's forces took Guatemala City: 'The city surrendered on 12 April and Morazan's soldiers entered it the following day, ending the civil war.'

wars.name: Central American civil war of 1838-1840
wars.outcome: The states declared independence one by one (Nicaragua, Honduras, Costa Rica in 1838; Guatemala by Carrera's decree of 17 April 1839; El Salvador in 1841).

certainty.note: The page gives the area but no boundary: the Belize coast was British-held, the Mosquito Coast was claimed but not held, and the Soconusco was claimed by Mexico (formal claim 1825) and Guatemala.
